title: sambucus racemosa var. callicarpa
intro: Sambucus racemosa var. callicarpa, commonly known as Black Elderberry, is a deciduous shrub native to North America, belonging to the Adoxaceae family. It has been used in traditional medicine for centuries, offering various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help alleviate symptoms of colds and flu, as well as provide relief from menstrual cramps and other discomforts. The therapeutic actions of Black Elderberry include antiviral, antipyretic, and anti-inflammatory effects, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, anthocyanins, and phenolic acids. These constituents may also contribute to the plant's potential in reducing inflammation and improving cardiovascular health.
